title: Chapter 6 — Shell Knock
description: Chuks recruits. A begging run goes wrong. The Hyenas beat Professor. Join the Tortoises, or stay independent.

cards.title: Day {stat:day}
cards.text: A man in a yellow shirt and brown trousers is drinking Mallam Garba's tea with his little finger raised. He knocks twice on his forehead when he sees you.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Ah, the famous one! Chuks. Smooth Operator. I represent a... society. A society of serious-minded gentlemen with excellent filing systems.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: (whispering) Tortoise. Yellow and brown. Dem slow, but dem no dey forget anything. Not even tea debt.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: No pressure. Today I just want to show you where real money lives. Zone 5. Rich people. Big gate. They give if you know how to ask.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Come. Watch and learn. Or learn and watch. Same thing.

options.text: "I go come alone. I no need escort."

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Rule of the gate: read the car before you open your mouth. Oga wants praise. Madam wants a story. Big boy wants a show. And some people...

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: ...some people you must not beg. Ever. Okay, oya. Show me.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Not bad. Not bad at all. You see? Alone, you beg. With brothers, people beg YOU. Think about it. Form T-12 is very short. Only nine pages.

beats.speaker: nephew
beats.text: You dey beg ME? Do you know who my uncle is? His face is on the rice! THE RICE!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His police escorts take your money, your dignity and one slipper. Chuks has vanished like a man with good instincts.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: (a text message, an hour later) Hon. Owó Ńlá is... less fond of you this evening. Please do not beg his family. It is bad for my filing.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: (reappearing) Ehen. That is why a man needs brothers. If you were a Tortoise, his escorts would have checked our register first. Think about it.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: You dey beg me? ME? My salary never enter since March. My daughter school fees dey look me like say I owe am. You dey beg ME?

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: (he laughs, the first real laugh you have heard from him) Lagos. Lagos is a joke with no punchline. Come. I go buy you akara. Don't tell anybody.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: I don write your face for my book. Next raid, I go find you first.

beats.objective: Hustle until night. (BEG AT THE GATE is open at Zone 5 now. Settlement's RALLY JOB too, if you work for him.)

cards.title: Night
cards.text: From Under-Bridge comes laughter. Not happy laughter. Hyena laughter. Then a scream you know.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: {name}! Dem don touch Professor! Purple shirts! Five of them! Dem laugh while dem dey beat am!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You find Professor under the flyover, curled around his missing fingers. A purple bandana lies in the gutter.

beats.speaker: nurse
beats.text: Professor. Again. That man fought more boxing in this hospital than in the ring. He will live. His pride, I am not sure.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (through a swollen lip) Rule number eleven... when the laugh is familiar... (he stops) No. Forget am. Na old man talk.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: One of them... I know that laugh. I taught that laugh to say 'Daddy'. Don't tell anybody, {name}. Swear.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: I brought pap and moi-moi for Professor. And for you, because you look like a man who has been crying in a toilet.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: {name}. Every day I see you, you dey run from something. Tell me the truth one time. Wetin you dey run from?

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (She waits. She is good at waiting.)

options.text: Tell her everything: Double-Double, Mama, the ₦850,000.
"I dey run from poverty. Like everybody."

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: ...Double-Double? The one with the dancing accountant in the advert? (She doesn't laugh. That is worse.) Okay. Okay. Then we have something to work on. You no go do am alone.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (she looks at you for a long time) Okay. When you ready to talk true, my shop dey there. Goodnight.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: (outside the hospital, under a streetlight, of course) Terrible thing. Hyenas have no respect. No paperwork. If Professor was a Tortoise, they would have needed a permit to touch him.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Join us. Protection for you. Protection for your people. Collections, raids, Task Force... the Shell covers all. And the Hyenas will think twice before they laugh near you.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (from the doorway) {name}. Whatever he is selling, ask for the receipt.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Two knocks on your forehead, and you're family. Or walk alone in this Lagos. Your choice, my brother.

options.text: Knock twice. Join the Iron Tortoises.
"I go stand on my own two legs."

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: Welcome, brother! Your initiation is on Friday. Study your answers. Wrong answers are... educational. Painful, but educational.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (from the hospital window, very quietly) Rule number twelve: the shell protects the tortoise. It also never lets him out.

beats.title: End of Act 2 — Shell Knock
beats.summary: You knocked twice. Money {money}. Tortoise loyalty {stat:cultLoyalty}. Hyena hatred {stat:rivalCultHatred}.

beats.speaker: chuks
beats.text: (he smiles like a man who has filed your name somewhere) No problem. The door is always open. Until it isn't.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (from the hospital window) Good. Now you have to be twice as smart, because nobody go cover your back. Except the people you help.

beats.title: End of Act 2 — Shell Knock
beats.summary: You stayed your own man. Money {money}. Goodwill {stat:communityGoodwill}. Hyena hatred {stat:rivalCultHatred}.
